note: Model calls run only on the server through OpenRouter. No model key is in browser code. The database is plain Postgres reached only from server code, so no database_rules labels apply. Tenant isolation depends on WHERE clauses in each route, and several routes miss them (see auth_gap). No committed .env and no real secrets. env.example holds placeholders. The widget uses /api/chat. /api/widget/chat is unused and fails on new chats because saveChat gets no orgId and puts a widget session id in a user FK. Config fields confidence_correction_threshold, correction_strategy and webhooks.completion_url do nothing: nothing reads the first two, and no code queues a conversation.completed job. Not reviewed: docs/, README.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .cursor/, drizzle/meta snapshots, components/ui (shadcn), lockfile.

labels.what: Chat ownership check only runs when both the caller and the chat have a userId. A widget session token from any org can post to any chat UUID, including another org's or a dashboard user's chat, and the model replies with that chat's full history. No orgId check either.
Any logged-in user from any org who posts to an escalated chat is saved with role agent and auto-assigned as the agent. There is no org membership or role check.
DELETE skips the ownership check when the caller is a widget session (userId null), so any widget token holder can delete any chat and its messages by id.
Live message stream checks only that the caller has some widget token or login. It never checks that the chat belongs to that session or org, so anyone can listen to any chat by UUID.
PATCH changes any chat's status by id for any logged-in user. No org membership check.

Customer email and name come from the embedding page (data-user-email) or a form with no verification. Any page can start a session that claims any customer's email, and the dashboard shows it as the customer.

When getActiveTools() is called with no orgId (widget chat route line 137), knowledge_search uses orgId null and searchKnowledgeBase (retrieval.ts lines 36-46) searches every org's documents. The widget chat route is broken for new chats, so reach is limited.

Route guard checks only that a session cookie exists and its matcher lists exact paths, so /dashboard/conversations, /dashboard/knowledge-base and /chat/[id] are not covered. Pages gate in client code only. Data APIs do check the session.
OrgMember has roles owner, admin and agent, but no route checks the role. Any member can delete knowledge sources and resolve chats.
escalate updates the status of whatever chatId the model passes and queues a webhook. No check that the chatId is the current chat or org, and no limit on repeat escalations.
collect_feedback inserts a feedback row for any chatId the model passes. Rating is bounded 1-5, but there is no check that the chat is the current one, no per-chat limit, and no comment length cap.
Code detects escalation keywords but only adds a prompt line telling the model to call escalate. Nothing escalates the chat if the model does not call the tool.
The current chat ID is given only in the system prompt. The escalate tool trusts whatever chatId the model sends and does not bind it to the request.
The current chat ID is given only in the system prompt. collect_feedback writes for whatever chatId the model sends.
Same keyword escalation done only as a prompt instruction in the widget chat route.
The model records a satisfaction rating it inferred, with no step where the customer confirms the score.

escalate queues a job with key type: escalation, but the webhook worker switches on job.data.event (webhook-worker.ts lines 17-33), so no escalation webhook is ever sent. The tool still tells the customer a human will follow up shortly.

Live handoff passes a message id string to emitChatMessage, which expects a message object. The stream listener (stream/route.ts lines 76-91) calls message.createdAt.toISOString(), throws, and swallows the error, so agent replies never reach the customer live. The comment says PostgreSQL NOTIFY, but chat-events.ts is an in-memory map.
Password reset email is not sent. The reset URL is written to the server console.
Verification email is not sent. The verification URL is written to the server console.
Edit profile Save Changes closes the dialog and shows an info toast. No API call is made.
Vote shows Upvoted or Downvoted for any HTTP response because toast.promise only fails on network errors. A 404 still shows success.
Resolve sets the status to resolved in the UI without checking the PATCH response.
Footer always says responses are verified by Vex in real time, but the chat route falls back to an unverified stream when Vex errors (route.ts lines 336-355).

OPENROUTER_MODEL defaults to openai/gpt-5-mini, while agent-config.ts line 43 defaults the model to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4. The chat routes never read OPENROUTER_MODEL, so the env.example value has no effect.
Embedding model hardcoded to openai/text-embedding-3-small. env.example sets OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL to text-embedding-3-large, which is never read and would not fit the vector(1536) column.

Vex agentId hardcoded to vex-customer-support here and at line 199, while config vex.agent_id defaults to my-support-bot (agent-config.ts line 78) and goes into webhook payloads. Two different ids for the same agent.

Widget hardcodes color #0066FF, bottom-right position, and always asks for email when none is given (line 466). The org config fields primary_color, welcome_message, position and require_email_if_anonymous are never sent to the widget.
Tool step limit stepCountIs(5) and reasoning effort high are hardcoded, repeated at lines 347-351 and 364-368 and in the widget route.
Retrieval topK 5 hardcoded here, with minSimilarity 0.3 default in retrieval.ts line 17.
Auth client falls back to http://localhost:3000.
Fallback origin http://localhost:3000.
Base URL falls back to http://localhost:3000.
Base URL falls back to http://localhost:3000.
Redis falls back to redis://localhost:6379. env.ts line 28 sets the same default.
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000.
Demo page loads the widget from http://localhost:3000 with a hardcoded org public key and a fixed test email.
Local Postgres with fixed dev_user/dev_password, published on host port 5432. Redis has no password and is published on 6379.

Server-side request forgery. The crawler fetches any user-supplied URL and follows redirects, with no block on private, loopback or cloud metadata addresses. The ingest route (ingest/route.ts lines 42-88) accepts any URL string.
Anyone with the public agent id from the embed script can mint unlimited widget sessions, and /api/chat has no rate limit. Strangers can spend the OpenRouter and Vex budget.
No size limit on uploaded file content and no page cap on sitemap crawls (crawl-worker.ts lines 158-189). Every chunk is sent to the paid embedding API.
Widget session token stored in localStorage on the host site, readable by any script on that page.
Widget session tokens never expire. lastActiveAt is updated but never checked.
Session token accepted in the URL query string, where it can land in logs and history.
First user message joined straight into the title generation prompt with no guard.
sendReasoning: true streams model reasoning to the browser, including widget customers. Reasoning can echo the system prompt and chat id. Also line 371 and the widget route line 159.
Password reset and email verification URLs with live tokens are written to server logs.
Public endpoint builds a fetch URL from the request origin, so a spoofed Host header makes the server send a GET to another host.
